implementation.name: OpenSCAD solid-model renderer
implementation.version_scope: Documentation as checked on 2026-10-13; no latest-version claim.

fit.text: Parametric solid models constructed from geometric primitives.

prerequisites.text: Learn dimensions, transformations and boolean operations.

execution.text: OpenSCAD evaluates .scad source into a model for preview/rendering.

behavior.text: Primitives and operations describe geometry; the source is not a general UI program.

tooling.text: The built-in editor and documented language operations support iterative modeling.

maintenance.text: Check render/export behavior and library versions before reusing models.

costs.text: COPYING includes GPL terms and a CGAL linking exception; external model libraries are separate.

example.run_instructions: Open block.scad in OpenSCAD and preview/render the model.
example.expected_result: Shows a centered rectangular solid measuring 20 by 10 by 5 model units.

implementation.name: Mozart 2 Oz programming system
implementation.version_scope: Documentation as checked on 2026-10-13; no latest-version claim.

fit.text: Oz programs run through the Mozart programming system.

prerequisites.text: Install Mozart's matching runtime/compiler; building requires its documented dependencies.

execution.text: The compiler creates code executed by the Mozart runtime.

behavior.text: Module functors import capabilities such as System for output and Application for process lifecycle.

tooling.text: The distribution includes runtime, compiler and an interactive programming environment.

maintenance.text: Choose a release for the target system rather than assuming an older Oz tutorial matches every tool.

costs.text: Mozart 2 source uses a two-clause BSD grant; optional components have independent notices.

example.code:
functor
import
    System
    Application
 define
    {System.showInfo "PLLDN"}
    {Application.exit 0}
end
example.run_instructions: With Mozart 2 installed, compile using ozc -c hello.oz -o hello.ozf, then run ozengine hello.ozf.

licenses.scope: The named implementation only; dependencies and host runtimes have separate terms.
licenses.notice: Retain source/binary notices; the grant does not identify all separately packaged components.

implementation.name: p4c P4_16 compiler frontend
implementation.version_scope: Documentation as checked on 2026-10-13; no latest-version claim.

fit.text: Packet-processing programs for a specified switch architecture.

prerequisites.text: Learn packet headers, parser states and the chosen target's architecture interfaces.

execution.text: p4c frontends check P4 source; target backends generate target-specific output.

behavior.text: Parser states extract header fields and transition to accept or reject.

tooling.text: The distribution includes p4test and target-specific compiler drivers.

maintenance.text: Target architecture and backend support must be checked before deploying a compiled program.

costs.text: The cited Apache license is part of p4c licensing; individual file notices and target SDK terms remain separate.

example.run_instructions: Use the p4test frontend with P4_16 mode to check the parser unit. A complete deployment also needs a target architecture, controls and a main package.
example.expected_result: Defines a parser extracting one byte; checking this unit is not a network deployment.

licenses.notice: Inspect per-file SPDX declarations; a license-text directory alone is not evidence for every target SDK component.

implementation.name: PHP 8.4 interpreter
implementation.version_scope: PHP 8.4 source-license scope and a command-line example; other releases must use their own distribution terms.

fit.text: Server-generated web content and command-line scripts; browser-side execution is a separate JavaScript context.

prerequisites.text: Begin with PHP syntax and variables; web applications additionally need HTTP, HTML and a web-server setup.

execution.text: The CLI needs a PHP interpreter; server-side use adds a web server and a PHP handler such as CGI or a server module.

behavior.text: PHP code produces output on its host; procedural and object-oriented styles are available.

tooling.text: The manual documents CLI use, database extensions, debugging extensions and the function library.

maintenance.text: Check the selected interpreter, server integration and installed extensions together before moving between deployments.

costs.text: Hosting and extensions are deployment choices; PHP distribution terms also include acknowledgement and naming conditions.

example.run_instructions: With a PHP CLI interpreter installed, run php hello.php. This example does not need a web server.
example.expected_result: Prints PLLDN followed by a newline.

licenses.scope: The PHP-8.4 branch's distribution grant; bundled extensions can have their own notices.
licenses.notice: Review acknowledgement and naming clauses; use the actual installed release's license.

implementation.name: ponyc compiler
implementation.version_scope: Documentation as checked on 2026-10-13; no latest-version claim.

fit.text: Actor-based applications with typed concurrent behavior.

prerequisites.text: Learn actors and reference capabilities; the compiler/runtime form a native toolchain.

execution.text: ponyc compiles a package directory into an executable.

behavior.text: The Main actor receives an Env containing standard input/output and arguments.

tooling.text: The tutorial provides installation, compilation and language chapters.

maintenance.text: Keep runtime and foreign-library requirements aligned with the target platform.

costs.text: The compiler's BSD-2-Clause grant is separate from native application dependencies.

example.code:
actor Main
  new create(env: Env) =>
    env.out.print("PLLDN")
example.run_instructions: Place main.pony in a hello package directory, run ponyc from that directory, then run the resulting executable.

implementation.name: PowerShell 7 on .NET
implementation.version_scope: Cross-platform PowerShell 7; Windows PowerShell 5.1 and OS-specific modules are different scopes.

fit.text: Automation and administration using structured objects; each operating system and installed module determines available operations.

prerequisites.text: Learn cmdlets, objects and pipelines rather than assuming a Unix text-only shell model.

execution.text: pwsh runs PowerShell code on .NET across supported Windows, Linux and macOS environments.

behavior.text: The pipeline passes .NET objects, preserving properties for filtering and composition.

tooling.text: Use cmdlets, modules and scripting support; module installation and target-service access are separate requirements.

maintenance.text: Check module and operating-system support when moving automation between hosts.

costs.text: PowerShell and the covered .NET runtime have MIT terms; external modules and hosted services need separate review.

example.run_instructions: With PowerShell 7 installed, run pwsh -File hello.ps1 where script execution is permitted by your administrator's policy. Do not change that policy for this example.
example.expected_result: Prints PLLDN followed by a newline.

licenses.notice: Retain applicable notices when distributing covered software; modules may differ.

licenses.scope: Runtime code covered by the repository's MIT grant.
